# Morphe

> Morphe is a functional, engine-agnostic Entity Component System for Clojure. Its public model is immutable world data transformed by ordered systems.

## Purpose

Morphe provides the state and execution model for a game or simulation. It does not try to be a complete game engine. Rendering, physics libraries, input devices, audio, windowing, asset loading, and the outer game loop belong at adapter boundaries.

The central operation is:

```clojure
(morphe.core/step runtime world dt commands)
```

It returns a map containing the next `:world` and transient `:events`. Given deterministic systems, the same world, commands, and timestep produce the same result.

Canonical architecture details live in [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md).

## Quickstart

The repository uses independent Clojure CLI projects under `modules/`:

```sh
cd modules/core
clojure -M:test
```

The Quil module tests use:

```sh
cd modules/quil
clojure -M:test
```

The LWJGL module tests use `clojure -M:test` with `-M:macos-arm64`, `-M:linux`, or `-M:windows` for native
artifacts. The repository root is a workspace coordinator and has no runtime dependency configuration.

The root build configuration is build-only. Use `clojure -T:build ci :version '"0.1.0-test"'` for the local pipeline,
`clojure -T:build jar` for lockstep module JARs, and `clojure -T:build deploy` for Clojars deployment.

The standalone platformer uses its own dependency project:

```sh
cd examples/platformer
clojure -M:run
clojure -M:test
```

## World and entities

`morphe.core/world` creates an immutable world containing entity IDs, component stores, and resources. An entity is only an identity. It has no behavior and can be represented as a generated integer.

Spawn an entity with component data:

```clojure
(let [[world player]
      (morphe.core/spawn
        (morphe.core/world)
        {morphe.components.2d/position-key
         (morphe.components.2d/position 0.0 0.0)})]
  ...)
```

Use `component`, `has-component?`, `add-component`, `set-component`, `update-component`, `remove-component`, and `destroy` through [morphe.core](modules/core/src/morphe/core.clj). Component writes return new worlds and reject dead entities.

Components are plain data stored under namespaced keywords. Component fields should also be namespaced by the component namespace. The built-in 2D component namespace defines position, velocity, acceleration, scale, rotation, and transform constructors in [components/2d.clj](modules/core/src/morphe/components/2d.clj).

Resources hold world-level data shared by systems. Use `get-resource`, `set-resource`, `update-resource`, and `remove-resource` for data such as input state, score, or simulation configuration.

## Queries

Queries select entities by component presence. Build them with [morphe.query/all](modules/core/src/morphe/query.clj):

```clojure
(q/all c2d/position-key c2d/velocity-key)
```

`query/all` supports required component keywords plus `query/optional` and `query/without` clauses. `query/query` returns matching entity IDs in sorted order. Queries inspect component presence, not component values.

## Systems

Systems are protocol-backed executable values defined in [morphe.system](modules/core/src/morphe/system.clj).

- `entity-system` runs an operation for each entity matching a query. Its operation receives `world`, `entity`, and `dt`.
- `system` runs one world-level operation. Use it for aggregation, resource updates, collision passes, or rules involving multiple entities.
- `command-system` handles selected command types before ordinary systems run.

An operation may return either a world or `{:world next-world :events events}`. Events are normalized into a vector and remain transient output from that step. Systems should keep pure data transformation separate from external effects.

System metadata can declare reads, writes, resource dependencies, and ordering constraints. The current runtime preserves the configured vector order; the `before` and `after` metadata records intent for scheduling and inspection.

## Commands and events

Commands are explicit input to a step. Create them with `morphe.core/command`:

```clojure
(ecs/command :game/move-forward {:entity player})
```

Command types must be keywords and payloads must be maps. A command system declares the command types it handles. This keeps external input at the edge and lets the simulation remain testable without a device or window.

Events are transient step results:

```clojure
(ecs/event :game/entity-defeated {:entity enemy})
```

Consumers such as audio, effects, or logging should process events outside the core world transformation. Events are not automatically stored in the next world.

## Runtime execution

[morphe.runtime/runtime](modules/core/src/morphe/runtime.clj) accepts either a vector of ordinary systems or a map with `:command-systems` and `:systems`:

```clojure
(def runtime
  (runtime/runtime
    {:command-systems [apply-input]
     :systems [movement collision]}))
```

`morphe.runtime/step` normalizes commands, processes every command system in order, then executes every ordinary system in order. Each system receives the world returned by the previous one. Ordering is behavior: movement must precede collision if collision should observe the new position.

## Engine boundary

The core namespaces do not depend on Quil or another renderer. An adapter consumes the world and translates external input into commands.

[morphe.adapters.quil](modules/quil/src/morphe/adapters/quil.clj) is an optional adapter in the Quil module that provides:

- A Quil window and frame loop.
- Held-key tracking as immutable data passed to `:command-fn`.
- Shape and sprite rendering from render-owned components.
- Asset loading from an explicit asset map.
- An optional `:overlay-fn` called after world rendering for text or HUD elements.

Start it with `quil/start!`, passing `:runtime`, `:world`, and optionally `:width`, `:height`, `:background`, `:assets`, `:command-fn`, `:event-fn`, and `:overlay-fn`.

[morphe.adapters.lwjgl](modules/lwjgl/src/morphe/adapters/lwjgl.clj) is an optional LWJGL 3 adapter in its own module. It provides a GLFW loop,
held-key polling, OpenGL 3.3 rendering for shared 2D shape/sprite data, and basic colored 3D cubes. Use
`morphe.components.render-2d` and `morphe.components.render-3d` for render data that stays independent of Quil.
The [LWJGL example](examples/lwjgl) demonstrates both dimensions.

## Platformer example

The [platformer README](examples/platformer/README.md) documents a complete small game. Its [game namespace](examples/platformer/src/platformer/game.clj) demonstrates:

- Marker components for players, platforms, coins, enemies, and goals.
- A normalized input command stored as a resource.
- Direct horizontal movement, gravity, jumping, and axis-aligned platform landing.
- Coin collection and score updates through entity destruction and resource updates.
- Enemy patrol, falling, goal detection, win/loss phases, and immutable restart by replacing the world.

The example keeps simulation logic independent from the Quil window. Its tests call `morphe.core/step` directly and inspect the returned world. The executable test entry point is [platformer.test-runner](examples/platformer/src/platformer/test_runner.clj).

## Design constraints

When extending Morphe, preserve these constraints from [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md):

- Keep persistent game state immutable and use plain Clojure data.
- Keep engine-specific concerns out of the core namespaces.
- Make time, randomness, and external input explicit resources or step inputs.
- Preserve old world snapshots after later transformations.
- Prefer simple data-oriented operations without sacrificing functional semantics.
- Add performance optimizations only when measurements justify them.
